title.narrative: Urban Water Supply and Sanitation Sector Project

description.narrative: The project will implement high priority components following the government’s water and sanitation sector plan to increase access to piped water supply and sanitation service, especially among the poor households; reduce reliance on groundwater and rainwater harvest and ensure more efficient use of water. The project will also enhance hygiene awareness, promote water conservation and improve fecal sludge management.

Progress Toward Outcome: (i)Water supply coverage and drinking water quality. Solomon Water (SW) has surpassed the project's water supply coverage target of 16,500 households with 16,705 households connected at the end of February 2024 representing an 86% increase in the number of connected households since project appraisal in May 2019. Over the 12 months since February 2023, SW has connected an additional 668 households to its water supply networks of which 94% (626 connections) were in the greater Honiara area. There have also been improvements in drinking water quality compliance with water safety plans across SW operations. (ii)Nonrevenue water reduction. Nonrevenue water (NRW) continues to be one of SW's greatest challenges. NRW across all SW water supply networks averaged 56.3% (or 1.07m3 per connection) in February 2024 marginally down from the national NRW average in August 2023 of 60.8% (1.20m3 per connection). The average NRW for the greater Honiara area in February 2024 was 56.6% (1.03m3 per connection). Overall, the project is off-track to reach the project NRW target in Honiara of 30% or less by 2027. Lack of progress on NRW is driven by primarily by aging infrastructure. Substantial investments are required to reduce NRW including expediting water main renewals. The project currently targets the replacement of 10km of trunk water mains in Honiara with high leakage. Investigations in 2022 indicate that about 50km of water mains in Honiara suffer substantial leakage and require replacement. Further investments are also required to reduce commercial losses (primarily illegal connections and water meters inaccuracies). (iii) Sewerage coverage. The respective targets of respectively increasing SW's sewerage coverage to 4,000 households, and the percentage of collected wastewater that is disposed through outfalls to 70% is off track given that the project's Honiara sewer expansion subproject has yet to commence. At end February 2024, 648 households were connected to the SW's sewerage networks down from 661 households in August 2023. Based on SW records, the 2019 baseline value of 1,000 households appears to be incorrect and requires amendment. While the project's ongoing sewerage contracts will address degraded coastal water quality issues in east Honiara, it is unlikely that the target number of households connected to the sewer network will be met. (iv)Onsite sanitation management. Progress towards achieving the target of 14,000 households in greater Honiara benefiting from improved onsite sanitation policies is on track following the preparation of the draft Greater Honiara Area Comprehensive Sanitation Plan 2022-2026. The draft Plan now requires ratification by Honiara City Council and Guadalcanal Province before the finalization of septage treatment plant design (design scheduled to be completed by Q3 2025). (v)Ambient Water quality at the Honiara Foreshore and in the Mataniko River. The water quality compliance target for sewage discharged from the Honiara sewer systems is likely to be achieved if the works to reconfigure the sewer system proceed. The design of the sewerage rehabilitation and outfall construction contract for the eastern-area system is current being reviewed by SW's engineering design consultant and procurement may proceed in Q1 2025. (vi)SW Financial sustainability. Full recovery of annual operation and maintenance costs, asset depreciation costs, and debt servicing costs from user charges and government community service obligation payments is essential for SW's financial sustainability. SW achieved full cost recovery in 2020 and just fell short of the target (by less than 3 percent) in 2021 and 2022. Further measures are required to improve the financial sustainability of SW including tariff adjustments and, equally importantly, further investments to reduce NRW.
